text:
maya: follow-up from RFC meeting 1: we need a runtime-friendly "quality envelope" attached to quant profiles. purpose: let runtime make O(1) safety decisions and choose fallbacks without heavy evals.
li: sounds useful. how's this different from the current profile?
maya: profiles today map ops->precision only. envelope = tiny, versioned contract with acceptance thresholds, ordered fallbacks, cost/latency weights, and rollout rules (canary/rollback). runtime reads cached envelope and does fast numeric checks.
zach: runtime constraints: no locks, mem-read only, sub-us checks. any per-request logic must be simple compares and a table lookup.
maya: agreed. plan: control-plane stores envelopes as small kv values (<1kb). runtime fetches envelope version id in startup and subscribes to invalidations. shadow-evals run async and propose patches.
ron: tenant overrides are the risky bit. sales will want cheaper options. how do we mitigate silent breakage?
maya: 3 mitigations: (1) safety_level enum (STRICT|CANARY|EXPERIMENTAL), (2) overrides require audit + approver, (3) default behavior is stepwise fallback not jump-to-fp32 unless expressly allowed.
li: can you paste a compact example we can iterate on?
maya: example (flattened string for readability):
```
profile_id=llama-3b-fp8-v1; safety_level=CANARY; allowed_loss_pct=1.3; max_coherency_drop=0.7;
fallbacks=fp8:int8:4bit:fp32; fallback_costs=0.0:0.12:0.35:0.6; latency_pen_ms=0:2:6:15;
canary_rate_pct=1; min_canary_samples=200; auto_rb_loss_pct=2.5; rb_window_min=30
```
li: ledger as colon-separated lists is cheap to parse. runtime can keep index of current mode and step along ledger.
zach: router needs to weigh envelope.cost vs request SLO. add per-fallback cost_penalty so routing can make trade-offs.
maya: yes, ledger entries will carry cost_penalty and latency estimate. router uses simple linear scoring: score = cost_penalty * cost_weight + latency_ms * latency_weight + quality_violation_flag * huge_penalty. pick lowest score mode that doesn't violate envelope thresholds.
ron: telemetry: what do we need to make envelopes meaningful?
maya: ship per-minute aggregates: loss_delta_pct, coherency_drop_pct, hallucination_spike_rate, canary_fail_rate. also emit chosen_fallback, envelope_version, override_tag in traces. make dashboards and alerts on canary_fail_rate and loss_delta_pct crossing thresholds.
li: baseline question: who computes baseline used to compute loss_delta_pct?
maya: baseline set by offline evaluator at profile publish. shadow-evals refine baseline and propose envelope version bumps. control-plane accepts version bumps when cohort stats are stable.
zach: multi-shard consideration: do we allow fragment envelopes per-shard/layer? runtime cost increases.
maya: add fragmentation flag in v2. default is per-profile coarse envelope. fragmentation allowed only if total envelope < 1kb and cache hit behavior is unchanged.
ron: RBAC + playbook?
maya: RBAC: only platform+sre can flip safety_level to EXPERIMENTAL. tenant requests for experimental require signed justification + ops ack and a monitored window. playbook: auto-rollback when auto_rb_loss_pct breached; otherwise page on-call with suggested rollback profile id and quarantine until shadow-eval completes.
li: action items recap:
- maya: PR for envelope schema + publish/override API (ETA 48h)
- zach: prototype runtime reader + lockless cache lookup + simple scoring (ETA 72h)
- ron: draft RBAC + ops playbook + rollback templates (ETA 48h)
- li: add telemetry fields + dashboard panels (ETA 24h)
dev-bot: created ticket 6230: quant-quality-envelope: schema + runtime cache + telemetry
li: one last practical item: add "override_reason" and "approver_id" strings to envelope metadata for auditability.
maya: done. we'll version v1 -> v1.1 with that field. thanks :rocket:
